references.text: Just before this, the crowd shouted, 'Away with this man!' ([ref:Luk 23:18|Luke 23:18]). The cry 'Crucify him, crucify him!' is an intensification of the same demand to take Jesus' life.
In [ref:Luk 23:23|Luke 23:23], it describes how the crowd continued to shout with loud cries and demanded that Jesus be crucified, and in the end they got their way.
In Matthew's parallel account, the crowd likewise shouts 'Crucify him!' when Pilate asks what he should do with Jesus ([ref:Matt 27:22-23|Matthew 27:22-23]).
Mark's parallel account describes the same cry from the crowd: 'Crucify him!' ([ref:Mark 15:13-14|Mark 15:13-14]).
In John's account, the chief priests and the guards shout 'Crucify! Crucify!' – the same double cry as in Luke ([ref:Joh 19:6|John 19:6]).
The crowd shouts again, 'Away with him, away with him! Crucify him!' ([ref:Joh 19:15|John 19:15]), showing the persistent and escalating hostility toward Jesus.
Peter later reminds the Jews that they denied Jesus before Pilate's face when he had decided to release him, and instead demanded that a murderer be freed ([ref:Apg 3:13-14|Acts 3:13-14]).
Paul refers to the event where the people of Jerusalem, although they found no guilt worthy of death in Jesus, asked Pilate to have him put to death ([ref:Apg 13:28|Acts 13:28]).

Isaiah's prophecy about the suffering servant foretold that he would be despised and rejected by people ([ref:Jes 53:3|Isaiah 53:3]). The crowd's demand for crucifixion is a fulfillment of this prophecy about rejection.
